claim: Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs) like DPO, which never train an explicit proxy reward model, still exhibit reward overoptimization/degradation as KL budget from the initial policy increases.
stance_target: the generality of Goodhart-style overoptimization beyond settings with an explicit learned reward model
scope_conditions: Direct Alignment Algorithms (DPO and variants) across objectives, training regimes, and model scales
quoted_support: "While the so-called reward hacking phenomenon is not well-defined for DAAs, we still uncover similar trends: at higher KL budgets, DAA algorithms exhibit similar degradation patterns to their classic RLHF counterparts."

claim: DAA methods can deteriorate before even a single epoch of the offline preference dataset is completed, indicating overoptimization can occur very early in offline-style training without iterated online sampling against a static proxy.
stance_target: overoptimization as a fast, offline-relevant phenomenon rather than one requiring extensive online exploration
scope_conditions: DAA training regimes studied in the paper
quoted_support: "we find that DAA methods deteriorate not only across a wide range of KL budgets but also often before even a single epoch of the dataset is completed"
